name: gaining
description: Something you had previously wanted is now yours.

variations.name: winning a game or contest
variations.description: Many contests involve an element of chance, so winning often comes with an element of pleasant surprise. If any skill was involved, it may come with some pride.

variations.name: winning an important contest you were favored to lose
variations.description: If you or your team were the predicted losers, a win may may affect perceived social status, provide a sense of triumph, or other positive experiences. It may come with gratitude.

variations.name: gaining a loved one
variations.description: It's not often we gain special relationships like friends, lovers, children, and pets. So when it happens, it may be cause for gratitude.

variations.name: gaining an important asset
variations.description: If something special is gained like a job or a house, it may cause pride, relief, and gratitude.

variations.name: gaining social status
variations.description: If the win comes with a perceived upgrade in social status, it will likely come with some rewarding brain chemicals.

variations.name: gaining something considered neutral or negative
variations.description: Phrases like 'gaining weight' and 'gaining enemies' are just double negatives -- these can be interpreted to mean 'losing fitness' and 'losing friends'.

commentaries.quote: When you've had a relatively easy life where you have most everything you really want, 'gaining' things seems like the norm. That can make 'not gaining' feel like 'losing', and actual loss feel intolerable.
It's not whether you win or lose, but how you play the game.

conditions: The state of the world changes in a way you perceive as positive.
